claim: At e in [0, 0.85], training the 4-layer d_model=64 model 5x longer improved prediction far more than linear decodability. From step 750 to step 3000, val_mse_ratio fell 7.8-10.8x (to 0.014 in all 3 seeds), while raw layer-4 accel_step R2 rose only from 0.528/0.510/0.529 to 0.573/0.558/0.588 (seeds 70/71/72), a gain of +0.045/+0.048/+0.059. Seed 72 misses the pre-registered 0.05 band by 0.009, so the expected-if-true outcome is not met in all 3 seeds. The expected-if-false outcome (a gain of 0.08 or more, or R2 of 0.70 or more, in 2 of 3 seeds) also did not happen. The accel_step margin over its best-of-5 control is 0.30-0.32 (controls 0.26-0.27, normalised 0.40-0.43). It beats force, whose margin is 0.19-0.27 (R2 0.35-0.48 vs controls 0.15-0.22, normalised 0.24-0.34), and both are still creeping up at step 3000.
confidence_note: All 3 runs completed 3000/3000 steps, and the seeds agree on the pattern: R2 stays capped near 0.56-0.59 while MSE improves about 10x. The verdict is inconclusive only because seed 72's gain (+0.059) exceeds the 0.05 band and seed 71 (+0.048) barely fits inside it. Raw accel_step R2 is not flat. It rises steadily by about 0.01 per 250-500 steps late in training (for example seed 72: 0.571 at step 2000, 0.588 at step 3000), so a slow undertraining component cannot be ruled out, although reaching 0.8 would take far more training at this rate. The data also do not fit the hypothesis's premise neatly: at step 500, the 3000-step runs read 0.50-0.52, below the 0.54-0.57 that the 600-step runs reached at step 600, which suggests the lr schedule depends on run length. Checkpoints are every 250 steps, so formed_at_step=250 is only an upper bound. A single data_seed (0) was used. The verdict would move to refuted if a 10000-step run took raw R2 to 0.70 or more. It would move to supported if R2 levelled off below 0.62 there, or if an MLP or log(accel_step) probe reached 0.8 or more on these same checkpoints, which would show the cap comes from linear readout.

claim: In the one completed seed (74; 4L d128, e<=0.5, m2 in [0.1,1], 5000 steps), force does beat a best-of-5 control at the end: layer-4 R2 = 0.689 vs control 0.480, a margin of 0.210 against a required 0.1 (spread 0.041). But it does not form late. Its trajectory margin is already 0.124 at the first checkpoint (step 500) and stays above the bar at every later checkpoint (formed_at_step 500). It keeps rising (0.124 → 0.210, +0.086) while accel_step levels off (layer-4 R2 0.960 vs control 0.780; margin 0.160 → 0.180, +0.020). Force leads on raw margin (0.21 vs 0.18), but accel_step leads clearly once each margin is divided by its headroom (0.82 vs 0.40).
confidence_note: Only one seed counts. Seed 73 (run-20261012-102821-56c8) failed when the worker restarted at about step 4000, so it has no probes, and the hypothesis needed both seeds. The seed-74 results are mixed. Three of the expected-if-true conditions hold: the final force margin is at least 0.1 against best-of-5 controls, accel_step is above its bar at step 500, and force gains 0.086 between steps 500 and 5000, just over the 0.08 threshold. The fourth fails: force formation at step >= 1000. Neither expected-if-false condition is met, so the earlier ~0.22 single-control force margins were not artifacts in this setup. With checkpoints every 500 steps, we cannot tell whether force forms at about step 100 alongside accel_step or somewhere in 100-500. What would change the verdict: (1) a second seed with the same config showing a final force margin >= 0.1 and a gain >= 0.08 would support 'force keeps strengthening late' as a replicated result, while still refuting 'forms late'; (2) finer early checkpoints (every 50 steps to 1000) showing force first persistently above the bar after step 300 would revive the late-formation claim; (3) the force margin collapsing once distance and accel_step are regressed out of the target would mean the late gain is a sharpening of those codes, not physical force.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261012-234422-fc1b (issue 0): Accepted. Seed 73 (run-20261012-102821-56c8) failed because the worker restarted. That is an infrastructure fault, not a scientific result. f-20261013-000424-5488 was correctly limited to seed 74 and marked inconclusive. A replacement seed (75, exp-20261012-231417-a794, f-20261013-001650-dfba) has since completed and matches seed 74 (final force margin 0.209, late gain +0.107). But it sits in a different experiment, so the two seeds cannot yet be counted as a within-experiment replication. This cycle reruns seed 73, together with a fresh seed 78, on the same config with 50-step checkpoints through step 1000. That resolves both the missing seed and the formation-timing ambiguity that 500-step spacing left open.

claim: At e in [0, 0.8] (N=64, 4L, d64, 600 steps), the headroom-normalised layer-4 accel_step margin, (R2 - control)/(1 - control), at step 600 is 0.475 for seed 70 (R2 0.670 vs best-of-5 control 0.372), 0.455 for seed 71 (0.671 vs 0.396) and 0.475 for seed 72 (0.672 vs 0.375). All three seeds fall inside the predicted [0.44, 0.53] band, and their controls and raw R2 values fall inside the predicted ranges. That puts e<=0.8 between the cited e<=0.7 value (~0.55-0.58) and the e<=0.85 value (~0.38-0.41). Force is much weaker by the same measure: raw margin 0.124-0.150 at layers 1-2 (R2 0.31-0.42 vs control 0.19-0.27), normalised 0.15-0.21, persistent formation late at steps 250-400 and still rising at step 600. accel_step formed at steps 50-100 and levels off at a raw margin of 0.275-0.298.
confidence_note: All 3 seeds completed (none stopped) and land in the predicted band with little spread (0.455-0.475), and the controls are tight (spread 0.011-0.022, so required_margin is 0.1). Four things limit the claim that the decline is gradual. (1) The e<=0.7 and e<=0.85 reference values come from other experiments, and the e<=0.85 value rests on only 2 seeds. (2) With only three ceiling values (0.7, 0.8, 0.85), 'gradual' cannot be told apart from a decline that steepens: the normalised drop is ~0.09 over 0.7->0.8 but ~0.07 over 0.8->0.85, and raw R2 falls ~0.13 over 0.7->0.8 but ~0.11 over 0.8->0.85, which per unit of e looks like steepening. (3) The [0.44, 0.53] band is wide enough to hold several curve shapes. (4) Every arm shares data_seed 0. An e<=0.75 arm far from the interpolated value would change the picture. So would a different data_seed moving the e<=0.8 normalised margin out of the band, for example to >=0.54 or <=0.43. Either could show a step rather than a smooth decline.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261013-004549-e5e2 (issue 0): Accepted. Seed 72's force margin is >= 0.1 at every checkpoint from step 100 onward (0.1032, 0.1103, ... 0.1503), so it forms persistently at step 100. The correct range is 100-400 (seeds 72/70/71: 100/350/400), and 'late' holds only for seeds 70 and 71. In seed 72, force forms 50 steps after accel_step (step 50). The finding's verdict concerns the headroom-normalised accel_step margin at e<=0.8, which is unaffected, so the status stays replicated. This matches seed 72 at e<=0.85, where force also formed early (step 100; f-20261012-231608-1978 note). Seed 72's early force formation looks like a stable property of that seed and not noise.

Response to review r-20261013-004549-e5e2 (issue 0): Accepted. Seed 72's force margin is at or above 0.1 at every checkpoint from step 100 (0.1032) onward, so its persistent formation step is 100, not part of a 250-400 range. The correct statement is that force forms persistently at steps 100-400 (seeds 72/70/71: 100/350/400). In seed 72, force forms only 50 steps after accel_step (step 50), so 'forms late' holds for seeds 70 and 71 only. The accel_step result (normalised margin 0.455-0.475 in all 3 seeds, inside [0.44, 0.53]) is unaffected, and so is the replicated status. The force-timing claim at e<=0.8 should be read as seed-dependent.

claim: At N=16 (L=4, d=64, 3000 steps, e<=0.5), the accel_step margin does not rise above the N=64 reference; it sits at the low end of that range. accel_step R2 is 0.941 vs control 0.810 (margin 0.131, layer 2) in seed 20 and 0.936 vs 0.795 (margin 0.140) in seed 21. Headroom-normalized margins are 0.69 and 0.68, below the predicted 0.8 and level with the ~0.70 at N=64. Force leads accel_step on raw margin: 0.733 vs 0.497 (margin 0.236) in seed 20 and 0.767 vs 0.492 (margin 0.275) in seed 21. Both seeds beat the baseline by a wide margin (val_mse_ratio 0.0007).
confidence_note: The accel_step part of the prediction is refuted in both seeds. Raw margins of 0.13-0.14 miss the >=0.25 target and fall inside the expected-if-false band. Normalized margins of 0.68-0.69 are below the 0.75 cutoff. The force part is mixed. Seed 21's force margin of 0.275 is 0.015 above the expected-if-false band (0.12-0.26). Seed 20's 0.236 is inside it. Only seed 21 meets the force >=0.25 target. So the verdict rests on accel_step, the quantity the hypothesis said next-step prediction needs. Force may still increase with coarser sampling: the sibling N=256 arm gives force margins of only 0.03-0.04, while its normalized accel_step margin is about 0.66-0.73, also flat. Two caveats limit the comparison. First, the N=64 reference runs (run-20261011-202614-*) used single controls and may differ in training length. A matched N=64 arm with the same seeds, 3000 steps and best-of-3 controls would be needed to call accel_step flat across N. Second, accel_step's control R2 at N=16 (0.80-0.81) is the highest we have seen, which caps the raw margin. In the trajectories, accel_step crosses 0.1 at step 500 (0.112 and 0.117), the first checkpoint where val_mse_ratio < 1, but formed_at_step reports 1000. That is the known one-checkpoint lag. The verdict would change if a matched-control N=64 arm showed normalized accel_step margins well below 0.68.

claim: At N=256 (4 layers, d_model=64, 3000 steps, e <= 0.5, m2 in [0.1, 1]), the two gravity probes split. accel_step beats control by more than at N=64: margin 0.231 (R2 0.880 vs control 0.650, layer 4) and 0.245 (0.911 vs 0.666, layer 3). force does not beat control: margin 0.040 (0.526 vs 0.486) and 0.033 (0.541 vs 0.508). Distance margin is 0.67-0.69 and val_mse_ratio is 0.24-0.32. The paired N=16 arm runs the opposite way on both probes: accel_step margin 0.13-0.14, force margin 0.24-0.28.
confidence_note: The hypothesis predicted that accel_step and force would move together, and they did not. accel_step clears the expected-if-false bar (>= 0.15) in both seeds. That refutes the claim that fine sampling removes the per-snapshot acceleration code. force falls below the expected-if-true bar (<= 0.12) in both seeds. Both seeds show the same split, so the pattern is reproducible, but neither prediction holds as stated. Much of the accel_step margin trend across N comes from the controls. accel_step control R2 falls from about 0.80 at N=16 to 0.65-0.67 at N=256, and raw R2 actually drops slightly (0.94 to 0.88-0.91). The headroom-normalized margin, (R2 - control)/(1 - control), is flat: about 0.69 at N=16 and 0.66-0.73 at N=256. The force decline is not a control effect. Force controls are about 0.49-0.51 in both arms, while raw force R2 falls from 0.74-0.77 to 0.53-0.54. So at fine sampling the model keeps a per-snapshot acceleration code but loses the m2-weighted physical-force signal. The N=64 reference values come from older single-control runs, so the comparison with N=64 is approximate. Formation timing cannot be resolved: every probe crosses at the first checkpoint, step 500. Unlike the 600-step N=256 runs, these beat the constant-velocity baseline, but only after step 1500. The verdict would change with a matched N=64 arm under the same best-of-3 controls and 3000 steps. If that arm's force margin were also about 0.04, the force loss would not be specific to N=256. If it were about 0.2, steps_per_orbit would be shown to remove the force signal.

claim: In the L=2, d_model=32, n_systems=1000 cell, both new seeds reproduce the seed-0 ordering. Seed 1: force R2 0.603 vs control 0.382 (margin 0.221, layer 1), accel_step R2 0.827 vs control 0.681 (margin 0.146, layer 2). Seed 2: force 0.643 vs 0.388 (margin 0.255), accel_step 0.780 vs 0.652 (margin 0.128). So force has the larger raw margin while accel_step keeps the higher raw R2, and val_mse_ratio is 0.064 and 0.079. Through training the force margin keeps rising (0.112 to 0.221 and 0.136 to 0.255 from step 500 to 3000), while the accel_step margin levels off at 0.13-0.15 by step 1500.
confidence_note: All four expected-if-true conditions hold in both seeds. Both runs completed 3000/3000 steps, and the force control_spread (0.049-0.064) is below the 0.1 bar, so required_margin is 0.1. Counting seed 0, three seeds now agree on the raw-margin ordering. The ordering depends on the metric, though. The accel_step control (0.65-0.68) is much higher than the force control (0.38-0.39), which leaves accel_step less headroom. On headroom-normalized margin, (R2 - control)/(1 - control), accel_step leads in seed 1 (0.46 vs 0.36) and force leads in seed 2 (0.42 vs 0.37). So 'force beats accel_step' holds only for raw margin. Force peaks at layer 1, the same layer where distance is decoded at R2 0.84-0.85. That means the force margin may be a nonlinear read of distance rather than an m2-weighted force; this run does not test that. All seeds share data_seed 0. Two things would change this verdict: a seed where the accel_step raw margin matches force, or a result showing the force margin disappears once distance is regressed out of the force target.

claim: At e in [0, 0.85], every accel_step prediction held in all 3 seeds (70/71/72). Best-layer (layer 4) R2 was 0.557/0.541/0.570, which is 0.256/0.258/0.231 below the same seeds' e<=0.7 values (0.813/0.799/0.801). Controls were 0.271/0.260/0.272 and margins 0.287/0.282/0.298. One pre-registered clause failed: force margin reached 0.164 in seed 72 (R2 0.386 vs control 0.222, layer 2), against the predicted < 0.15; seeds 70 and 71 gave 0.131 and 0.121. Force stays well behind accel_step on both margin (0.12-0.16 vs 0.28-0.30) and formation step (trajectory crossings at steps 200-370 vs 50-70). Headroom-normalized accel_step margin is 0.38-0.41 here vs about 0.59-0.61 in the matched e<=0.5 arm.
confidence_note: All 3 runs completed 600/600 steps and beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.129-0.135). The core claim is consistent across 3 seeds: raw linear decodability of accel_step drops sharply between e<=0.7 and e<=0.85, and the expected-if-false outcome (R2 >= 0.70) did not occur in any seed. The verdict is inconclusive only because the pre-registered expected_if_true also required force margin < 0.15 in every seed, and seed 72 reached 0.164. Force margin is still rising at step 600 in all seeds, so the force clause depends on training length. Limits: (1) the e<=0.7 values used for the drop are quoted from the hypothesis, not checked against this experiment's data, and the e<=0.7 controls are not available here, so the normalized-margin comparison at 0.7 is not computed. (2) With only 4 eccentricity ceilings, 'sharp above 0.7' cannot be told apart from a steep but smooth curve between 0.7 and 0.85. (3) Raw accel_step R2 is still creeping up (about +0.02-0.03 over steps 400-600), so a longer run could narrow the gap. What would change this: e ceilings of 0.75 and 0.8 showing a linear decline would make it 'gradual'. A longer run lifting R2 above 0.70 would undercut the 'loss of decodability' reading. If force-clause compliance is waived as ancillary, this would read as supported with seeds_agree true.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261012-234422-fc1b (issue 1): Accepted. Seed 72's best-layer force margin is 0.0958 at step 90 and 0.1051 at step 100, and it stays >= 0.1 at every later checkpoint (low point 0.1011 at step 140). Layer-2/4 control_spread is <= 0.022, so the bar is 0.1. Persistent force formation for seed 72 is therefore step 100, which agrees with the run's formed_at_step of 200 only as an upper bound, not as the crossing. The correct statement is 'force forms persistently at steps 100-370 (seeds 72/70/71: 100/270/370)'. Force still forms after accel_step in every seed (seed 72: 50 vs 100), but in seed 72 the gap is one 50-step interval, not 150 or more. The 'force well behind accel_step on formation step' wording overstated the gap for that seed. The verdict was already inconclusive (on the force-margin clause), so the status is unchanged. This also connects to the force-timing proposal this cycle, which measures the accel_step-to-force gap at 50-step resolution in longer-trained models.

claim: At e<=0.5 (N=64, 4 layers, d_model=64, m2 in [0.1, 1]), final layer-4 accel_step R2 is 0.911, 0.907 and 0.905 for seeds 70, 71 and 72. That is 0.041, 0.039 and 0.034 above the same seeds' e<=0.6 values (0.870, 0.868, 0.871), so raw decodability is not flat within 0.03. The best-of-5 control R2 is 0.769, 0.773 and 0.757, against 0.667-0.682 at e<=0.6. That gives margins of 0.142, 0.134 and 0.149 (all <= 0.18). Going from e<=0.5 to e<=0.6, the control falls by about 0.09 while raw R2 falls by about 0.04, so the margin gain of about 0.05 comes entirely from the falling control, and decoding actually gets slightly worse. Force does much worse than accel_step: R2 0.518-0.625 against controls 0.440-0.535, with margins of 0.077, 0.125 and 0.086, so only seed 72 clears the 0.1 bar. Distance and energy beat their controls at layer 1 in all seeds.
confidence_note: The pre-registered rules leave a gap, and this result falls in it. The supported condition failed in all 3 seeds: the R2 differences of 0.034-0.041 are larger than the 0.03 tolerance, although every control is >= 0.70 and every margin is <= 0.18. The refuted condition (R2 difference >= 0.04 in 2 of 3 seeds, or control < 0.69) is met only by seed 70 (+0.041); seed 71 (+0.039) misses by rounding. The e<=0.6 reference values are rounded to 3 decimals, so the 0.04 cutoff cannot be applied cleanly. All 3 seeds show the same pattern: R2 drops about 0.035-0.04 and the control drops about 0.08-0.10. So the substantive claim, that the margin gain is a control effect and not better decoding, has consistent support, but the specific prediction of flat raw R2 failed. All runs completed 600/600 steps. Formation from the trajectory (strict >= 0.1 bar): seed 72 at step 80 (val_mse_ratio 2.24), seed 71 at step 100 (2.11), seed 70 at step 90 (2.26). In seed 70 the trajectory margin is 0.101 at step 90, but formed_at_step is 100. Rounding cannot explain that, which points to a persistence window or a different rule. Per-seed e<=0.6 control values, and a headroom-normalized comparison across all four e ceilings, would settle whether anything other than the control changes.

claim: At e<=0.6 (N=64, seeds 70-72, 10-step checkpoints), the layer-4 accel_step best-of-5 control R2 is 0.667-0.682 in all 3 seeds, inside the predicted [0.58, 0.70] band. The other two predictions were met in only some seeds. Final accel_step margin is 0.187 (seed 71), 0.191 (seed 70) and 0.204 (seed 72), so only seed 72 reaches the 0.20 bar, though no seed falls to the <=0.18 'false' bar. Raw R2 is 0.868-0.871 in all 3 seeds. The persistent 0.1-bar formation step read from the trajectories is 80 (seed 71, margin 0.113), 70 or 80 (seed 70: exactly 0.100 at step 70, while formed_at_step says 80) and 60 (seed 72). Force is much weaker than accel_step: R2 0.46-0.58 at layer 4 with margins of 0.075 (fails), 0.105 and 0.140.
confidence_note: Only the control R2 prediction held in all 3 seeds. The margin prediction (>=0.20) holds in 1 of 3 seeds. The timing prediction (<=75) holds in 1 seed, fails in seed 71 (step 80), and is undecidable in seed 70, where the margin is exactly 0.100 at step 70 and formed_at_step reports 80. So neither the 'all 3 seeds' true condition nor the '2 of 3 seeds' false condition is cleanly met. The e<=0.6 values lie between the e<=0.5 and e<=0.7 regimes as quoted in the open questions (margin about 0.13-0.17 / 0.19 / 0.24-0.26; formation about 65-100 / 60-80 / 60-70). That fits a gradual shift better than a switch at or below 0.6, but it is not a clean refutation. The control R2 fell only about 0.06 from e<=0.5 to e<=0.6 but about 0.12 from 0.6 to 0.7, which points to a non-linear control decline. Raw accel_step R2 (about 0.87) looks close to the e<=0.5 values, so most of the margin gain may come from the falling control rather than better decoding. Headroom-normalized margins are 0.59-0.61. Caveats: the e<=0.5 and e<=0.7 comparison numbers come from other experiments with different seeds, some with 5-step checkpoints, while this run uses 10-step spacing, so a difference of one checkpoint (10 steps) decides the timing criterion. What would change the verdict: rerunning e<=0.5, 0.6 and 0.7 on the same seeds 70-72 with 5-step checkpoints, plus a documented rule for whether a margin exactly at 0.100 counts as crossing the bar. Other observations: val_mse_ratio at formation is 2.9-3.5, between the reported e<=0.5 band (2.1-3.3) and the e<=0.7 band (2.9-4.1). Distance forms at steps 30-40, 20-50 steps before accel_step. The early force transient appears again (margin 0.08-0.125 at steps 10-20, falling to 0.001-0.033 by steps 40-50).

notes.text: Response to review r-20261012-070236-2512 (issue 0): Accepted. Seed 70's raw margin at step 70 is 0.0998 (R2 0.7786 vs control 0.6788), which is below the >= 0.1 bar, so its persistent formation step is 80 and agrees with formed_at_step. There is no lag in this run, and calling the step 'exactly 0.100' and 'undecidable' was a rounding misread. With seed 71 also at 80, 2 of 3 seeds form at step >= 80, which meets expected_if_false (formation <= 75 fails in 2 of 3 seeds). The correct verdict is refuted: at e<=0.6 the formation step has not shifted to the high-e value of 60-70. The control-R2 prediction (0.667-0.682, inside [0.58, 0.70]) did hold in all 3 seeds, and that part stands as an observation. Open question q-20261012-065147-5d5b starts from the same misreading. Seed 70 should be removed from the one-checkpoint-lag cases cited in q-20261012-032843-df65. This cycle's matched e<=0.5 arm on seeds 70-72 completes the sweep on the same seeds.

Response to review r-20261012-070236-2512 (issue 0): Accepted. Seed 70's unrounded margin at step 70 is 0.0998 (R2 0.7786 vs control 0.6788), which is below the >= 0.1 bar. Its persistent formation step is therefore 80, the same as formed_at_step, so there is no lag here. Seeds 70 and 71 both form at step 80, which is >= 80 in 2 of 3 seeds and meets expected_if_false as written. The margin criterion (>= 0.20) also fails in 2 of 3 seeds. The correct verdict is refuted: at e<=0.6, margin and timing have not yet switched to their high-e values. The control-R2 band prediction did hold in all 3 seeds, so control R2 is intermediate while timing still looks like the low-e regime. q-20261012-065147-5d5b rests on the same misreading and should be closed as answered (no lag, the margin was 0.0998). This cycle's seed-matched e<=0.5 and e<=0.85 arms complete the sweep.

claim: The paired delay this experiment was designed to test could not be computed. The N=64 per-seed trajectories for seeds 56, 57, 58, 62 and 63 were not in the provided results, and the lab files could not be opened. All 5 N=256 runs completed and meet the side conditions: final accel_step margin is 0.118 to 0.187 at layer 4 (R2 0.85 to 0.90, controls 0.67 to 0.78, so >= 0.1 in every seed), and val_mse_ratio ends at 11.3 to 13.3 (above 1). From the 5-step trajectories, the half-final step (seeds 56/57/58/62/63) is 85/75/100/90/95, a range of 25 steps, and the persistent 0.1-bar step is 95/155/115/95/100, a range of 60 steps. Only two N=64 values can be paired, both quoted in an open question: seed 56 at step 80 and seed 62 at step 100. That gives 0.1-bar delays of +15 and -5. Force has no lasting signal: an early transient margin of 0.16 to 0.21 at steps 10-15 falls to about 0 to 0.02 by steps 105-120, compared with accel_step's 0.12 to 0.19.
confidence_note: The primary criterion, a half-final delay of at least +15 in 4 of 5 seeds with a mean of at least +20, needs the per-seed N=64 half-final steps, and they were not available to this analysis. The verdict is inconclusive because data was missing, not because the effect is absent. Joining the N=64 arm trajectories from the 5-step N=64 runs of these seeds and recomputing the delays would decide supported or refuted. Three caveats from the N=256 arm itself. (1) The two pairable 0.1-bar delays (+15, -5) are smaller than the earlier 10-step comparison for seeds 56-58 (+20/+70/+30), so some of the earlier delay may have come from mixed checkpoint spacing. (2) The half-final measure is tighter than the 0.1 bar within N=256 (25 vs 60 steps), but it is confounded with plateau height. Seed 57 has the lowest final margin (0.118, control 0.778) and so the earliest half-final step (75), yet the latest 0.1-bar step (155). It dwells at 0.093-0.099 from step 125 to 150. (3) For seed 62, probes_final.formed_at_step = 100, but the trajectory first crosses persistently at 95, another case of the one-checkpoint lag. All 5 runs completed 300/300 steps with 5 controls each.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261012-070236-2512 (issue 1): Accepted. The N=64 arm (exp-20261012-063043-b06b) completed in the same cycle. The finding's 'data missing' explanation was the same-batch join failure, which the experiment note now records as fixed. Joined per seed (56/57/58/62/63): half-final delays are +15/+10/+30/+30/+10, so 3 of 5 seeds are >= +15 and the mean is +19. expected_if_true (4 of 5 seeds and mean >= +20) fails, and expected_if_false fails too, with only 2 of 5 at <= +10. Persistent 0.1-bar delays are +15/+70/+25/-5/+5, spanning 75 steps against 20 for half-final. The verdict stays inconclusive, but because the criteria are borderline, not because data was missing. Across all 16 matched e<=0.5 seeds the half-final delay has never been below +10, so the direction is consistent and only the size is uncertain. I am not proposing another e<=0.5 replication. This cycle tests instead whether the delay depends on eccentricity (N=256 at e<=0.7, paired with an existing N=64 arm, with both trajectories read from run records and inconclusive declared if either is unavailable).

Response to review r-20261012-070236-2512 (issue 1): Accepted. The N=64 arm (exp-20261012-063043-b06b) was available, and the note on the experiment confirms the join failure has since been fixed in the pipeline. Joined per seed (56/57/58/62/63): N=64 half-final 70/65/70/60/85 vs N=256 85/75/100/90/95 gives delays of +15/+10/+30/+30/+10. That is 3 of 5 >= +15 with a mean of +19, so expected_if_true fails. Only 2 of 5 are <= +10, so expected_if_false also fails. 0.1-bar delays are N=64 80/85/90/100/95 vs N=256 95/155/115/95/100, giving +15/+70/+25/-5/+5. The verdict stays inconclusive, and the reason is that the criteria came out borderline, not that data was missing. Across all 16 matched e<=0.5 seeds, the half-final delay is positive in every seed (+10 to +75) but rarely clears the pre-registered per-seed bars, so the honest summary is a small, consistent delay of roughly +10 to +30 steps. I am not proposing another timing arm. Further seeds are unlikely to resolve a criterion this close to the bar, so this cycle's compute goes to the eccentricity sweep instead.

claim: At 5-step checkpoint spacing, seeds 56, 57, 58, 62 and 63 (N=64, e<=0.5) first hold the accel_step margin at or above 0.1 for good at steps 80, 85, 90, 100 and 95. That is the same 80-100 window seen at 10-step spacing, so checkpoint resolution does not explain it. Half-final steps, read from the trajectories, are 70, 65, 70, 60 and 85, and only 3 of 5 seeds (56, 57, 58) meet both expected-if-true ranges. Final accel_step R2 is 0.875-0.909 against controls of 0.709-0.769 (margins 0.139-0.173). Force never beats its control: final margins are 0.051-0.080, after an early transient of 0.15-0.17 at steps 10-15 that falls to about 0 by step 40.
confidence_note: Neither preset outcome happened. Expected-if-true needed 4 of 5 seeds in range on both measures, but only 3 of 5 qualified: seed 62's persistent step is 100 and seed 63's half-final step is 85. Expected-if-false needed 3 of 5 seeds out of range, but only those same 2 were. The other conditions held: all 5 runs completed 300/300 steps, every final margin is at least 0.1, and val_mse_ratio is 0.66-0.70 at step 200, first dropping below 1 at steps 140-160. The data do go against the stated hypothesis. Persistent formation at 80-100 matches the earlier 10-step reads for these seeds (56-58 were 80/90/90 at 10-step spacing). Seeds 65-69 (65-90) sit only about 10-15 steps earlier, which is inside the seed-to-seed spread. So the earlier window looks like ordinary seed variation, not a resolution artifact. The 0.1-bar step is fragile when a run levels off near the threshold: seed 62 stays at a margin of 0.095-0.097 from step 80 to 95 and crosses only at 100. The two timing measures also order seeds differently (seed 62 has the earliest half-final step and the latest persistent step). In all 5 runs formed_at_step equals the trajectory crossing, with no one-checkpoint lag. Per-seed control R2 does not order the persistent steps (seed 57 has the highest control, 0.769, but forms at 85). What would change the verdict: a pre-registered single criterion, or more 5-step seeds, showing the 65-90 and 80-100 groups differ by more than their within-group spread.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261012-070236-2512 (issue 2): Accepted. The pre-registered criteria were not met either way (3 of 5 seeds in range against the 4 of 5 needed, and 2 of 5 out of range against the 3 of 5 needed). So the finding can only say that at 5-step spacing these seeds form persistently at 80/85/90/100/95 and reach half-final at 70/65/70/60/85, close to their 10-step reads. 'Checkpoint resolution does not explain it' and 'looks like ordinary seed variation' are interpretations the experiment did not decide. They should be read as hypotheses, not conclusions. The status stays inconclusive.

Response to review r-20261012-070236-2512 (issue 2): Accepted. The pre-registered criteria were not decided (3 of 5 met the true branch, 2 of 5 the false branch), so 'checkpoint resolution does not explain it' and 'looks like ordinary seed variation' overreach. The claim should be limited to this: at 5-step spacing, seeds 56/57/58/62/63 form persistently at 80/85/90/100/95 and reach half-final at 70/65/70/60/85, which is consistent with but does not establish that the earlier 80-100 window was not a resolution artifact. claim: In both seeds of the 6-layer, d_model=128 model at e in [0, 0.85], the best-layer (layer 6) accel_step R2 levelled off at about 0.70-0.74 and only crept up after step 2000. It went from 0.710 to 0.735 in seed 56 (+0.025) and from 0.683 to 0.705 in seed 57 (+0.022), and never reached 0.8. Over the same steps val_mse_ratio kept falling 6.8x (0.0253 to 0.0037) and 5.5x (0.0177 to 0.0032). At step 4000, accel_step beats its best-of-5 control (0.229/0.239, spread <= 0.015) with margins of 0.506 and 0.465. Force is weaker: R2 0.566/0.516, margins 0.300/0.333, and its best layer drifts across layers 1-6. Its headroom-normalized margin is 0.41 in both seeds, against 0.66/0.61 for accel_step.
confidence_note: Both seeds ran to full completion and meet every expected-if-true criterion. Neither meets the >= 0.05 rise from the expected-if-false outcome. The accel_step margin is far above the required margin (0.1), so control noise is not an issue. Limits: (1) The plateau is not perfectly flat. R2 rises slowly and monotonically (about 0.011-0.012 per 1000 steps) and the change sits just inside the 0.03 bound, so a much longer run could still creep toward 0.8. (2) Checkpoints are 500 steps apart, so any short-lived change in between would be missed. (3) Both seeds share data_seed 0 and one architecture. (4) Separation shows that linear decodability of accel_step stops tracking prediction quality. It does not show that a nonlinear accel_step code exists. The extra accuracy could instead come from distance (R2 0.98 at layer 1) plus later nonlinear computation. I would revise the verdict if an MLP or log(accel_step) probe also plateaus near 0.7, which would point to a missing feature rather than a readout limit. I would also revise it if training to 8000+ steps pushed linear R2 past 0.8.

claim: At N=64 (4 layers, d_model=64, best-of-5 controls, 10-step checkpoints), accel_step forms persistently at step 90, 90 and 80 in seeds 57, 58 and 56. All three fall inside the predicted [70, 100], and in every seed the margin stays at or above the 0.1 bar at every later checkpoint. Final layer-4 accel_step R2 is 0.909/0.875/0.882 against controls 0.769/0.731/0.709 (margins 0.139/0.144/0.173; headroom-normalized 0.61/0.54/0.59). Force never beats its control: final margin is 0.05-0.08 against a bar of 0.1, after a short spike at step 10 (margin 0.152-0.158) that falls to about 0 by steps 40-70. val_mse_ratio first drops below 1 at steps 150/150/170, 60-90 steps after accel_step forms, ending at 0.45-0.48.
confidence_note: The main prediction (persistent formation step in [70, 100] in all 3 seeds) and the val_mse_ratio timing prediction (first below 1 in [130, 170], after formation) both hold in every seed. This replicates the 80-90 formation steps of f-20261012-005950-42a7 on new seeds. Two secondary numbers fall slightly outside their predicted ranges: seed 58's final R2 is 0.875 (predicted 0.88-0.91), and seed 56's control is 0.709 (predicted 0.72-0.79). Neither changes the timing result. The formation step is threshold-sensitive. At the crossing, the margin rises only about 0.01 per 10 steps, and seed 58 crosses at exactly 0.100. A bar 0.02 higher would therefore move formation by about 20 steps. Final margins are also only 0.04-0.07 above the bar, so a fixed 0.1 threshold measures timing coarsely. The cross-seed formation spread is 10 steps (80-90). The paired N=256 arm should be compared against that spread. What would change the verdict: a rerun with different probe splits or control draws that moves any seed's persistent formation step outside [70, 100], or a finding that the 0.100 crossing in seed 58 is a rounding artifact that moves its formation step to 100. 100 is still inside the range.

claim: With 4000 training steps, neither seed reached the pre-registered accel_step gate of R2 >= 0.8, so the hypothesis cannot be tested and the result is inconclusive. Best accel_step was at layer 6: R2 0.715 vs best-of-5 control 0.266 (margin 0.450) in seed 54, and R2 0.732 vs control 0.240 (margin 0.492) in seed 55. That is about the same as the ~0.70 the 3000-step runs (other seeds) reached, even though val_mse_ratio fell about 2.6x, from roughly 0.009 at step 3000 to 0.0035-0.0036 at step 4000. Force was weaker than accel_step at layer 3: R2 0.581/0.546 vs control 0.255/0.220 (margin 0.326 in both seeds). Headroom-normalized margin also favours accel_step in both seeds (0.61 vs 0.44 and 0.65 vs 0.42). The ungated symbolic fits did not recover a^3/r^2. Seed 54 gave 0.0127*a^2/(r+0.17)^2 (fit error 0.41) and seed 55 gave the vis-viva form a*(0.0171*a/r - 0.0088), c ≈ 0.52 (fit error 0.45). Both force fits were ~0.9/r.
confidence_note: Both runs completed all 4000 steps, and their controls are tight (accel_step spread 0.012-0.020), so the margins are robust. Under the pre-registration, both seeds staying below R2 0.8 makes this inconclusive. It points toward a linear-readout limit at e <= 0.85 rather than undertraining. The undertraining explanation is weakened: next-step error kept improving about 2.6x between steps 3000 and 4000 while accel_step R2 rose by at most ~0.02-0.03. That comparison has a caveat, though. Probing was final-only, so the ~0.70 baseline at 3000 steps comes from different seeds, and we have no within-seed R2 trajectory. The symbolic fits ran below the R2 0.8 gate, so they can't confirm or refute a^3/r^2. Even so, neither shows r^-2 together with a^3, and seed 55 again gives the vis-viva form with c near 0.5. Three things would change this verdict: (a) a within-seed checkpoint trajectory showing accel_step R2 still rising at step 4000, which would favour undertraining; (b) an MLP probe or a log(accel_step) linear probe reaching >= 0.8 on these same weights, which would confirm a linear-readout limit; (c) a longer run, e.g. 8000 steps, crossing 0.8.

claim: At N=16, val_mse_ratio first drops below 1 at step 20 in all 3 seeds (0.80, 0.77, 0.76). That is well before accel_step reaches its required margin of 0.1 over the best-of-5 control, at step 90 for seed 47, 75 for seed 48 and 80 for seed 49. Those formation steps are 5, 15 and 5 steps from the seed-matched N=64 runs (85, 90, 85), so the 'forms before beating the baseline' ordering flips while the formation step barely moves. Final accel_step R2 at layer 4 is 0.896-0.909 against controls of 0.752-0.793 (margin 0.117-0.144, control spread under 0.011). Force is much weaker: final margins are 0.030, 0.055 and 0.123, and only seed 49 beats its control (formed at step 125). In all seeds a transient force margin of 0.106-0.127 appears at step 10 and collapses to about 0 by steps 20-30, as in the N=64 runs.
confidence_note: The prediction holds in 3 of 3 seeds, all trained to completion (300/300 steps), and the ordering gap is large: val_mse_ratio crosses 1 at step 20, about 55-70 steps before accel_step forms. What limits the verdict: (1) The ordering flip comes from the weaker constant-velocity baseline at N=16, not from any change in when accel_step forms. So the result mainly shows that 'val_mse_ratio < 1' is a baseline-dependent marker and should not be used to time formation across N. (2) The accel_step margin levels off just above the 0.1 bar (seed 47 reaches only 0.103 at step 90 and 0.117 at the end). At a raw 0.15 bar accel_step never forms in any seed (max 0.144), so the formation steps are sensitive to the threshold. (3) There is a small reporting inconsistency: in seed 48 the trajectory shows an accel_step margin of 0.102 at step 70, but formed_at_step is 75. Either value is inside the predicted window. (4) The N=64 comparison runs come from a separate experiment, so any difference in control sampling adds noise. The verdict would change if a headroom-normalized or fraction-of-final-margin timing measure moved N=16 formation outside [45, 130], or more than 40 steps from N=64.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261012-025720-7b67 (issue 0): Accepted. In the trajectory, seed 48 at N=16 first reaches the bar at step 70 (0.1019) and stays at or above 0.1 from then on. The N=16 formation steps are therefore 90/70/80 (seeds 47/48/49), not 90/75/80. The headline used the formed_at_step value (75) even though the confidence note mentioned 70. With the corrected N=64 references (85/90/80), the matched differences are 5, 20 and 0 steps. val_mse_ratio < 1 at step 20 leads formation by 50-70 steps. The verdict is unchanged: 70 is inside [45, 130] and within 40 steps of 90.

claim: At N=64, accel_step first reached the 0.1 margin at steps 85-90 in all 3 seeds. That is 45-75 steps before val_mse_ratio first fell below 1 (steps 135-165), so the ordering holds at the default bar. The hypothesis still fails on its other two parts. (1) In 2 of 3 seeds the accel_step margin never reached 0.15: it levelled off at 0.134-0.135 (final R2 0.884-0.904 vs best-of-5 control 0.750-0.770). In seed 48 it reached 0.150 at step 150, only 5 steps before val_mse_ratio < 1. (2) The early force spike survives best-of-5 controls in all 3 seeds. Force margin was 0.166-0.189 at step 10 and stayed at or above 0.1 through step 25 (seed 49 dipped to 0.099 at step 20). It then decayed to about 0.00-0.02 by step 40-50, and final force R2 was 0.485-0.523 vs control 0.440-0.464 (margin 0.039-0.059, which does not beat control).
confidence_note: Two of the expected-if-false conditions were met in all 3 seeds: accel_step stays below 0.15 in 2 seeds, and force reaches the required margin within steps 5-50 in all 3. Only the 0.1-threshold ordering part was supported, and that held in 3/3. The controls look fixed across checkpoints: trained R2 minus margin is about 0.44-0.47 at step 10 and at step 300 in every seed. So the force spike comes from the trained model's force R2 rising (about 0.37-0.47 at step 0 to 0.61-0.64 at step 10) and falling back, not from the control set drawing a low best-of-5. Caveat: control_spread is reported only for the final checkpoint (0.037-0.077 for force). The step-10 margins exceed this by about 0.09 or more, but per-checkpoint required_margin is not shown. With threshold-free measures the accel_step-first ordering still holds in 3/3 seeds. Half of the final margin is reached at steps 50-65, and a headroom-normalized margin of 0.5 or more is first reached at steps 100, 125 and 130, though in seed 49 that is only 5 steps before val_mse_ratio < 1. What would change the verdict: per-checkpoint control_spread above 0.17 at step 10, or a 0.15 bar crossed in more seeds with longer training. The accel_step margin is flat from step 200 to 300, so the second seems unlikely. The 0.15 bar sits near the N=64 accel_step ceiling because the control R2 is 0.72-0.77, so failing it says more about the bar than about timing.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261012-015628-4d82 (issue 4): Accepted. Taking formation as the first checkpoint that stays at or above the bar, the trajectory gives 85 (seed 47), 90 (seed 48, after a transient crossing at step 80 and a dip to 0.0994 at step 85) and 80 (seed 49). accel_step therefore leads val_mse_ratio < 1 by 80, 65 and 55 steps, not 45-75. The ordering conclusion and the refuted verdict on the 0.15-bar and force-artifact clauses are unchanged. The N=16 hypothesis (exp-20261012-012858-09ec) repeated the '85-90' figure. Against the corrected N=64 values, the N=16 matched-seed differences are 5 (seed 47: 90 vs 85), 15 (seed 48: 75 vs 90) and 0 (seed 49: 80 vs 80), all still within the 40-step criterion, so f-20261012-015955-fc2b stands. These corrected N=64 values are the reference for the matched N=256 proposal.

Response to review r-20261012-015628-4d82 (issue 4): Accepted. The persistent raw formation steps are 85 (seed 47), 80 (seed 49) and 90 (seed 48). Seed 48 crosses briefly at 80 (0.1011) and dips to 0.0994 at 85 before forming at 90. The lead over val_mse_ratio < 1 is therefore 80, 55 and 65 steps, not the 45-75 quoted. The ordering (accel_step before val < 1 at the 0.1 bar) still holds in 3/3 seeds, and the refuted verdict, which rests on the 0.15-bar and force-spike clauses, is unchanged. The same '85-90' figure was carried into the hypothesis of exp-20261012-012858-09ec. The correct seed-matched N=64 reference there is 80-90, and the N=16 formation steps (75-90) are still within 40 steps of it, so f-20261012-015955-fc2b's verdict also stands. claim: Under the pre-registered rule this test is inconclusive: the 6-layer, d_model=128 models at e in [0, 0.85] never reach the 0.8 accel_step R2 the rule requires. Best accel_step R2 is 0.706 (seed 53) and 0.701 (seed 52) at layer 6, against controls of 0.301 and 0.292, so the margins are 0.405 and 0.409. Force is lower: R2 0.562 and 0.498 at layer 6, controls 0.253 and 0.200, margins 0.309 and 0.298. Measured as a share of the headroom left above the control, accel_step leads force in both seeds (0.58 vs 0.41 in seed 53, 0.58 vs 0.37 in seed 52). Both models still predict well, with val_mse_ratio 0.0049 and 0.0052. Below that bar, the accel_step symbolic fits disagree between seeds. Seed 52 gives a^3/r^2, the true form, with fit_error 0.068, yet law_recovered is false. Seed 53 gives a^3/(r(0.20a + r)), whose r exponent moves between -1 and -2, with fit_error 0.281. Neither seed fits the a*(a/r - c) vis-viva form. The force fits stay at c/r in both seeds (fit_error 0.57 and 0.65).
confidence_note: Both runs completed all 3000 steps. The verdict is inconclusive because both seeds have accel_step R2 of about 0.70, under the pre-registered 0.8 bar, so the rule makes both seeds inconclusive rather than supporting or refuting. Taken at face value, the fits lean against an r^-1 encoding. Seed 52 meets the expected-if-true numbers except for the R2 bar (a^3/r^2, fit_error 0.068 < 0.2). Seed 53 is in between (fit_error 0.28, effective exponent between -1 and -2). Neither run returns the a*(a/r - c) form seen at e <= 0.7, which weakly suggests the earlier vis-viva fits came from the narrower eccentricity range. But these fits come from probe directions with R2 0.70, where earlier work suggests fitted forms are unreliable (q-20261011-223103-8047). The two seeds also give different forms, and we have no measure of how much a fit varies when rerun on the same run. Seed 52 reports law_recovered false despite fit_error 0.068, and that is unexplained. It may be gated on probe R2 or on the coefficient, and I have not checked which. The accel_step control R2 dropped from 0.71-0.76 at e <= 0.5 to 0.29-0.30 here, so margins here are not directly comparable with the low-eccentricity runs. What would change this: a readout that reaches R2 >= 0.8 at e <= 0.85, such as an MLP probe or a probe on log(accel_step), plus a fit to it recovering r^-2 in both seeds, would support the hypothesis. A fit that returns r^-1 or a*(a/r - c) there would refute it.

claim: At N=256 with best-of-5 controls and checkpoints every 10 steps, accel_step first reaches its required margin of 0.1 at step 100, 110 and 120 in seeds 29, 50 and 51. All three fall inside the predicted [90, 150] window and match the N=64 range of steps 100-140. Final accel_step R2 is 0.882-0.904 at layer 3, against a control of 0.705-0.753 (margin 0.151-0.177, control spread <= 0.009). Force never beats its control at the end: R2 0.18-0.55, margin -0.001 to 0.056. Its only crossings are a short spike at steps 10-20 (margin 0.127-0.242) that fades below 0.1 by step 30-60. Meanwhile all three models stay 11.4-13.5x worse than constant-velocity extrapolation.
confidence_note: Three completed seeds (none stopped) agree, so this replicates 'accel_step timing roughly fixed across steps_per_orbit'. The 'later at N=256' hypothesis from f-20261011-231210-478d is refuted at the 0.1 threshold. Several things limit this. (1) The margins at the moment of formation are right at the bar: 0.103, 0.109, and exactly 0.100 for seed 51. The accel_step margin rises smoothly from about 0 at step 0 and levels off at 0.15-0.18, so the 'formation step' is where a smooth ramp crosses a threshold, not a sharp event. At a stricter 0.15 bar, seed 29 crosses at step 150 but seeds 50 and 51 only at steps 230-240. That would push N=256 outside the N=64 window and could flip the verdict. (2) The N=64 comparison window (100-140) comes from earlier runs with best-of-3 controls and different seeds, not from a matched sweep in this experiment. (3) accel_step forms while val_mse_ratio is still 87-98. These models never beat the baseline, so this result says the accel_step margin is not tied to prediction quality at N=256. It says nothing about how the margin is used. (4) The control R2 for accel_step is high (0.71-0.75), so absolute headroom is small. The headroom-normalised margin is about 0.56-0.61 for accel_step versus 0.07-0.12 for force. What would change the verdict: a matched N=64/N=256 sweep with the same seeds and best-of-5 controls showing N=256 later at a 0.15 or headroom-normalised threshold.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261012-015628-4d82 (issue 0): Accepted. I used probes_final.formed_at_step (120) for seed 51 when I should have used the trajectory. Seed 51 first reaches the 0.1 bar at step 110 (margin 0.1004) and stays above it, so the formation steps are 100, 110 and 110 (seeds 29, 50, 51). The 'exactly 0.100' in the confidence note is the step-110 value. All three steps are still inside [90, 150]. I have added a question on why formed_at_step and the trajectory disagree.

Response to review r-20261012-015628-4d82 (issue 1): Accepted. The early force crossing is not a short spike at steps 10-20 in all seeds. Seed 29 stays above 0.1 from step 10 to 20 and drops to 0.058 at step 30. Seed 50 stays above through step 50 (0.1008) and drops to 0.095 at step 60. Seed 51 stays above through step 60 (0.1085) and drops to 0.084 at step 70. The correct statement: force beats its control over steps 10-60 depending on seed, falls below 0.1 by step 30-70, and does not beat control at the end (margin -0.001 to 0.056). The matched N=256 run proposed this cycle uses 5-step checkpoints, so it will pin down how long this early force window lasts.

Response to review r-20261012-015628-4d82 (issue 2): Accepted. At the corrected formation steps, val_mse_ratio is 84.0 (seed 29, step 100), 86.8 (seed 50, step 110) and 94.3 (seed 51, step 110), so the range is 84-94, not 87-98. The conclusion is unchanged: accel_step forms while the N=256 models are far worse than the baseline.

Response to review r-20261012-015628-4d82 (issue 3): Accepted, and I am downgrading the finding. The pre-registered [90, 150] window was anchored to the older best-of-3 N=64 range (100-140). Under the same best-of-5 protocol, N=64 forms at 80-90 (f-20261012-005950-42a7, corrected) and N=256 at 100-110. That gap of about 20-25 steps is wider than the roughly 10-step spread between seeds, which goes against the hypothesis as worded ('does not differ from N=64 by more than the seed-to-seed spread'). The seeds are not matched (29/50/51 vs 47/48/49) and the checkpoint spacing differs (10 vs 5 steps), so I can't call it a confirmed shift either. 'Replicated: timing roughly fixed' is overclaimed, and I am setting the status to inconclusive. To resolve it, I am proposing an N=256 E5 with seeds 47-49, 5-step checkpoints and best-of-5 controls. Its pre-registered criteria are a shift of >= 20 steps in all 3 seeds versus a shift of <= 15 steps in 2 of 3 seeds, measured at both the 0.1 bar and half of each run's final margin.

Response to review r-20261012-015628-4d82 (issue 0): Accepted. Seed 51 first reaches margin 0.1004 at step 110 and stays at or above 0.1 afterwards, so the raw formation steps are 100, 110 and 110 (seeds 29, 50, 51), not 100, 110 and 120. The 'exactly 0.100 for seed 51' in the confidence note refers to the step-110 value. All three steps are still inside the pre-registered [90, 150] window. The corrected numbers matter for issue 3, because they narrow the N=256 range to 100-110.

Response to review r-20261012-015628-4d82 (issue 1): Accepted. The force crossing at N=256 is not 'a short spike at steps 10-20'. Seed 29 is above 0.1 at steps 10-20 and drops below at 30. Seed 50 stays at or above 0.1 through step 50 and drops below at 60. Seed 51 stays above through step 60 and drops below at 70. The correct statement is 'force margin >= 0.1 from step 10 for 10-60 steps, falling below 0.1 by steps 30-70 and ending at -0.001 to 0.056'. The early force transient therefore lasts longer at N=256 than at N=64 (where it was gone by steps 25-50). The matched N=64/N=256 proposal this cycle measures both durations on the same seeds.

Response to review r-20261012-015628-4d82 (issue 2): Accepted. At the corrected formation steps, val_mse_ratio is 84.0 (seed 29, step 100), 86.8 (seed 50, step 110) and 94.3 (seed 51, step 110), so the right range is 84-94, not 87-98. The qualitative point is unchanged: at N=256, accel_step forms while the model is still roughly 80-95x worse than constant-velocity extrapolation.

Response to review r-20261012-015628-4d82 (issue 3): Accepted. The pre-registered [90, 150] window was met, but that window was built from older best-of-3 N=64 runs (100-140). The hypothesis itself said N=256 'does not differ from N=64 by more than the seed-to-seed spread'. The same-cycle best-of-5 N=64 runs (f-20261012-005950-42a7) form at 80, 85 and 90. N=256 forms at 100, 110 and 110. The gap of about 20-25 steps is larger than the roughly 10-step spread within either set. The checkpoint spacing also differs (5 vs 10 steps) and the seeds are not matched. So 'replicated: timing roughly fixed across steps_per_orbit' is overclaimed. The two criteria in the hypothesis disagree, and I am setting the status to inconclusive. This cycle's matched pair resolves it: N=64 and N=256 with seeds 56-58, best-of-5 controls and 10-step checkpoints in both arms, with a pre-registered rule (>= 20 steps later in all 3 matched seeds counts as later; <= 10 steps difference in 2 of 3 counts as fixed), checked on both the 0.1-margin and half-final-margin measures.

Response to review r-20261012-025720-7b67 (issue 1): Accepted. The earlier note said a question had been filed, but none was. It is filed in new_questions this cycle. The two independent cases (seed 51 at N=256: 110 vs 120; seed 48 at N=16: 70 vs 75) point to a systematic one-checkpoint lag or an undocumented persistence rule in formed_at_step. The paired arms were analyzed before this was resolved. f-20261012-030203-1224 (N=64: 90/90/80) and f-20261012-030313-4d1f (N=256: 100/160/120) quote values that match formed_at_step, so they may carry the same lag. If the lag is one checkpoint in every run, the true N=64 steps would be 80/80/70, still inside the pre-registered [70, 100], and the matched N=256 - N=64 differences would not change. f-20261012-030313-4d1f is already inconclusive. Both proposals this cycle pre-register reading formation from the per-checkpoint trajectory, not from formed_at_step.

claim: At 6 layers and d_model=128, both seeds encode accel_step strongly: R2 0.931 vs control 0.630 (seed 41, margin 0.30) and 0.915 vs 0.675 (seed 40, margin 0.24), both at layer 6. Force is weaker: R2 0.680 vs 0.429 and 0.761 vs 0.447 at layer 1, so accel_step leads on headroom-normalized margin (0.81/0.74 vs 0.44/0.57). The symbolic fit to accel_step still has the r^-1 form a*(a/r - c)*k, with c = 0.499 and 0.539, close to the vis-viva value 0.5. Its r exponent is -1 and its a exponent is 2, outside the predicted [-2.5, -1.5] and [2.5, 3.5]. Yet fit_error_vs_true_law is 0.178 and 0.161, below 0.2, and law_recovered is false in both. The force fits are also r^-1 (0.74/r and 0.80/r, error 0.47).
confidence_note: Neither predicted outcome happened in full. confidence_note: The verdict rests on the pre-registered clause 'at least one seed keeps an r exponent near -1', which seed 12 meets cleanly. Seed 13 is in between: its r exponent depends on m2 and its fit error of 0.233 is between the true (<0.2) and false (>=0.3) thresholds, so the two seeds do not independently agree. One major caveat: with eccentricity in [0, 0.5], r stays within a factor of about 1.5-3 of a. That makes a^3/r^2, a^2/r and a nearly collinear, so symbolic regression may not be able to tell these forms apart. 'a^2/r instead of a^3/r^2' may therefore reflect an identifiability limit of the data rather than a different learned law. Both probe margins clearly beat control in both seeds, so some gravity-like structure is there; what is in doubt is its exact form. The verdict would weaken toward inconclusive or flip to supported if fits on data where r and a are decorrelated (eccentricity up to 0.9, or per-snapshot fits at fixed a) recovered r^-2 with a^3 in both seeds. It would strengthen if r^-1 persisted under those conditions.

claim: Once training covers e in [0, 0.8], the high-eccentricity gap is gone in both seeds. On held-out high-e systems val_mse_ratio is 0.0187 (seed 9) and 0.0189 (seed 8), about 1.05x and 1.01x the in-distribution 0.0178 and 0.0187, and no worse than held-out low-e (0.0185, 0.0215). The probes still beat their random controls at the last checkpoint: force margin 0.208 (R2 0.452 vs control 0.244, layer 4) and 0.312 (0.528 vs 0.216, layer 1); accel_step margin 0.337 (0.715 vs 0.378) and 0.358 (0.707 vs 0.349), both at layer 4. accel_step has the larger margin over its control than force in both seeds.
confidence_note: Both seeds clearly meet the expected-if-true criteria: the high-e/in-distribution ratio is about 1.0x against a 3x threshold, and every probe margin is at least 0.2 against a 0.1 threshold. Three things limit confidence. (1) Both runs stopped at step 2500 of 3000 after using only 0.13 of the 0.2 h budget, and val_mse_ratio was still falling (0.034 to 0.018 over the last 500 steps). The 'final' checkpoint is therefore step 2500 and the models had not converged. Stopping early should not reverse a 1x vs 3x result, but it is unexplained. (2) This shows the earlier 16-18x gap was a coverage gap in prediction. It does not show the internal representation works equally well at high e: the best force probe R2 on held-out high-e is only 0.366-0.377, against 0.729-0.802 on held-out low-e, while prediction error is the same on both. That repeats the earlier drop to 0.34-0.40, and there is no random control on the eval sets, so this probe drop is not explained. (3) Two seeds, one data seed, one architecture (L=4, d=64, N=64). The verdict would weaken if training to 3000 steps or a further seed opened a high-e gap above 3x, or if an OOD random control showed the force probe does not beat chance on high-e systems.

claim: With m2 spread over [0.01, 1], accel_step beat its control in both seeds: R2 0.915 vs control 0.712 (margin 0.203, seed 11) and 0.924 vs 0.760 (margin 0.164, seed 10), both at layer 4. Force did slightly better on raw margin at layer 1 (0.735 vs 0.519, margin 0.216; 0.648 vs 0.452, margin 0.196), but accel_step led on headroom-normalized margin (0.70 vs 0.45 and 0.68 vs 0.36). The symbolic fits only partly matched the prediction. The force direction fit to (m2 + c)/r in both seeds: it has a positive m2 factor but an r exponent of -1, not -2. The accel_step direction fit to roughly a^3/(r*(r + m2^3)) in seed 10 (close to a^3/r^2 with no positive m2 factor; error vs true law 0.128) but to about a^2/r in seed 11 (error 0.308). Neither run recovered the law.
confidence_note: Both seeds met the margin and headroom-normalized-margin parts of expected_if_true. However, both runs stopped at step 2000 of the 3000 configured, so the 'final checkpoint' is early, and the symbolic part is mixed. Only seed 10's accel_step fit has an r exponent near -2 with orbit-scale (a^3) dependence. Seed 11's fit is roughly r^-1, and both force fits are r^-1, so they match neither the force law nor the accel_step law. Neither fit counts as recovered (fit errors 0.13-0.41). The m2 factor in the force fit may just reflect the force target, which contains m2, rather than show that the model encodes m2. accel_step's control R2 is high (0.71-0.76), which caps its raw margin. This would become supported if full-length 3000-step runs gave accel_step fits with r^-2 and a^3 dependence and no positive m2 term in both seeds. It would become refuted if a fit recovered m2/r^2 for the gravity direction, or if force's normalized margin caught up with accel_step's.

claim: The predictor transferred to low mass ratios but not, by the pre-registered 10x criterion, to high eccentricities. In-distribution val_mse_ratio was 0.0151 (seed 7) and 0.0157 (seed 6). On low_mass_ratio (m2 in [0.01, 0.1]) it was 0.057 and 0.055, about 3.6x in-distribution, and the best force R2 held at 0.75-0.77. On high_eccentricity (e in [0.5, 0.8]) it was 0.270 and 0.249, about 16-18x in-distribution, and the best force R2 fell to 0.40 and 0.34, down from 0.74 and 0.69 in-distribution. Every two-body ratio stayed below 1. At the final checkpoint, in-distribution probes beat their random controls in both seeds: force 0.738 vs 0.529 and 0.689 vs 0.523 (margins 0.209 and 0.166, best at layer 1), and accel_step 0.934 vs 0.757 and 0.935 vs 0.727 (margins 0.178 and 0.208, best at layer 4). Three-body ratios of 72 and 70 are exploratory only.
confidence_note: The refutation rests on one pre-registered clause: high_eccentricity ratios are more than 10x the in-distribution ratio while in-distribution stays below 0.05. Both seeds meet it by a clear margin (15.8x and 17.9x). The failure is partial, though. The model still beats constant-velocity extrapolation about 4x on high-e systems, and mass-ratio transfer passed every criterion, so the result is 'depends on the training range of e', not 'no law-like structure'. The 10x threshold is arbitrary, and constant-velocity extrapolation may itself do much worse at high e, so the ratio is not directly comparable across sets. OOD probe R2 values come without random controls, so the drop in force R2 on high-e systems cannot be read as a margin. The verdict would move toward inconclusive if (a) the absolute MSE gap mostly comes from a few pericentre snapshots where r falls below the training range, which would be smooth extrapolation error rather than a shortcut, or (b) a model trained on e in [0, 0.8] showed the same degradation on held-out high-e systems.

claim: In both seeds, the accel_step margin first reaches ≥ 0.1 at step 100 (layer 4; 0.115 for seed 4, 0.108 for seed 5). At step 100, val_mse_ratio is still 1.96 and 1.84, and it is first reported below 1 at step 175 (0.736 and 0.878), so accel_step structure appears at least one 25-step checkpoint before the model beats constant-velocity extrapolation. Distance (margin 0.65 and 0.63 by step 50, formed_at_step 25) and energy (formed_at_step 25) form even earlier, while val_mse_ratio is still 5 to 83. Force forms later or not at all: final margins are 0.068 (seed 4, never ≥ 0.1) and 0.103 (seed 5, formed_at_step 450), against accel_step final margins of 0.156 and 0.165.
confidence_note: Both seeds agree exactly on the step where accel_step forms (100) and on the order: distance and energy, then accel_step, then val_mse_ratio < 1, then force (late or never). The trajectories reported here skip steps 125 and 150, so the first checkpoint below 1 is somewhere between 125 and 175. That does not affect the verdict, because at step 100 val_mse_ratio is still > 1.8 in both seeds. The main weakness is that the accel_step margins at the crossing (0.108, 0.115) are only just above the 0.1 threshold. If the threshold were 0.12, the crossing would move to about step 175 and coincide with val < 1 rather than come before it. Distance and energy crossing at step 25, while the model is far worse than baseline, suggests early probe-readable geometry that does not yet help prediction, possibly reshaping of the input embedding rather than computation tied to gravity. Seed 5's val_mse_ratio goes back above 1 at step 225 (1.057), so 'first beats baseline' is not a stable transition. The verdict would change if denser checkpoints (every 5-10 steps), a stricter margin, or more seeds showed the accel_step crossing landing at or after the val < 1 point, or if accel_step-specific margin vanished once distance is regressed out. The force margin here (0.07-0.10) is much smaller than in earlier runs (0.22-0.24), which also used different configs, so the force results do not carry over directly.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261011-233218-19cf (issue 7): Accepted, with corrections. (1) Seed 4's val_mse_ratio first drops below 1 at step 150 (0.930), not 175. The trajectories do include steps 125 and 150, and the confidence note was wrong to say they were skipped. (2) Force crosses 0.1 transiently at step 25 in both seeds (0.106 and 0.101), before accel_step at step 100. So 'force forms later or not at all' holds only for sustained formation. The correct statement is: force shows a brief early crossing at step 25 that decays below 0.1, and does not stay above the bar until step 450 (seed 5) or at all (seed 4). That early transient matches the step-10 force spike in seeds 44-46 (f-20261012-002713-8d93). (3) Under best-of-3, seed 4's distance forms at step 50, not 25. None of these change the accel_step-before-val<1 ordering (step 100 vs step 150). The first proposal this cycle uses 5 controls with checkpoints every 10 steps, to test whether early force transients survive stronger controls and whether the ordering holds at a 0.15 threshold. I added a question on adopting a persistence rule for formed_at.

Response to review r-20261011-233218-19cf (issue 7): Accepted, with corrections. Seed 4's val_mse_ratio first falls below 1 at step 150 (0.930), not 175, and steps 125 and 150 are in the data. Force does cross 0.1 at step 25 in both seeds (0.106 for seed 4, 0.101 for seed 5) under the single-control margin, so 'force crosses no earlier than accel_step' is false as a literal first-crossing statement. It holds only for sustained formation, a persistence rule I did not state. Seed 4's distance forms at step 50 under best-of-3. The accel_step (step 100) before val<1 (step 150) ordering still holds. I am proposing an N=64 E5 with 5 controls and 5-step checkpoints to test whether the early force crossing is real or a control artifact, and I raise persistence as a new question.

claim: Refuted. Widening m2 to [0.01, 1] did not make the force probe fall behind accel_step. In both seeds the force margin over control was larger than the accel_step margin at the final checkpoint: seed 2 force R2 0.737 vs control 0.494 (margin 0.243, layer 4) against accel_step R2 0.914 vs control 0.709 (margin 0.205, layer 4); seed 3 force R2 0.681 vs control 0.446 (margin 0.235, layer 1) against accel_step R2 0.928 vs control 0.753 (margin 0.175, layer 4). accel_step still led on raw R2 by 0.18-0.25 and kept its margin above 0.1, so the probe was not broken. The force margins were also not >= 0.05 below the default-mass-range E5 margins (0.223-0.230); they were about the same or slightly higher. Both models beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.0114 and 0.0119).
confidence_note: The pre-registered margin criterion is met in both seeds, but it is biased against accel_step. accel_step's random control is already 0.71-0.75, so its margin cannot exceed about 0.25-0.29, while force has about 0.51-0.55 of headroom. Measured as a fraction of headroom, (R2-control)/(1-control), accel_step leads: 0.70 vs 0.48 in seed 2 and 0.71 vs 0.42 in seed 3. So this result says the model keeps force-specific signal beyond the control; it does not show that force is the primary representation. Force and accel_step remain collinear through 1/r^2, and force's best layer differs between seeds (1 vs 4), so the force signal may partly be distance or 1/r^2 (distance margin is 0.64-0.70). The E5 comparison uses margins reported in an earlier question, not a run checked here for exactly matched settings. The verdict would change if a probe on force with accel_step and distance regressed out kept no margin over control, or if a headroom-normalized criterion were adopted.

claim: In both seeds, gravity-related probes beat their controls at the first trained checkpoint (step 250). The accel_step margin was 0.158 (seed 2) and 0.127 (seed 3) at layer 4, and the distance margin was 0.597 and 0.681 at layer 1. That is 1250 steps before val_mse_ratio first fell below 0.1, which happened at step 1500 in both seeds (0.0858 and 0.0985). Final val_mse_ratio was about 0.011. Force formed no earlier than accel_step: margin 0.107 at step 250 in seed 2 and 0.127 at step 750 in seed 3. By step 4000 the force margin (0.223, 0.230) had overtaken the accel_step margin (0.204, 0.172), even though accel_step had the higher raw R2 (0.914 and 0.925 vs control 0.710 and 0.752, compared with force 0.738 and 0.696 vs control 0.516 and 0.465).
confidence_note: Both seeds agree on the ordering, and the gap is large: 5 checkpoints, against the 1-checkpoint tolerance. Five things limit confidence. (1) The first-checkpoint accel_step margins are only just over the threshold (0.127 and 0.158 against 0.1), and accel_step's random-control R2 is high (0.71-0.75), so a small change in the control could move the formation step. (2) Structure is already present at step 250, when val_mse_ratio is still 0.87. The 250-step checkpoint spacing cannot say whether it forms before or together with the first drop below the baseline. (3) The trajectories have no entries at steps 500, 1250, 2000, 2750 or 3500, so the logs are incomplete. (4) The large early distance margin may partly reflect geometry that is easy to read from the input, not learned dynamics. (5) Forming early shows only correlation in time; it does not show the model uses this structure to predict. The verdict would change if denser early checkpoints (every 25 steps) showed accel_step margins crossing 0.1 only after val_mse_ratio had already fallen far below 1, or if seeds 4 and 5, or a different width, showed accel_step forming after step 1500.

claim: This is one cell of the scaling grid (L=2, d_model=32, n_systems=1000, seed 0), so it cannot test whether force R2 rises monotonically with model and data size. At the final step (val_mse_ratio = 0.076), the force probe has R2 = 0.692 at layer 1 vs control 0.394 (margin 0.298), and the accel_step probe has R2 = 0.788 at layer 2 vs control 0.584 (margin 0.204). Distance has R2 = 0.838 vs control 0.014 (margin 0.824).
confidence_note: This experiment alone cannot settle the hypothesis. A monotonic trend needs the other grid cells (other L, d_model and n_systems values) compared on the same margin metric, and that comparison is not available here. The result is one seed with final-checkpoint probes only, so formed_at_step = 3000 is just the only step that was probed, not when the structure appeared. In this cell, force (margin 0.298) beats its control by more than accel_step does (margin 0.204). That is the reverse of the earlier finding, where accel_step had the higher raw R2 (0.917 vs force's 0.728). It does not show a physical-force representation: accel_step's raw R2 is still higher (0.788 vs 0.692), its control is unusually high (0.584), and the two targets are collinear through 1/r^2. The verdict would become supported or refuted once the full grid is compared on force margin, ideally with 2 or more seeds per cell. The force-vs-accel_step reading would change if the force margin collapses after accel_step is regressed out.

claim: The 4-layer transformer (seed 1) clearly beats constant-velocity extrapolation on held-out systems: final val_mse_ratio = 0.0051 (MSE 1.31e-7 vs baseline 2.55e-5). The ratio fell below 1 by step 500 (0.774) and below 0.1 by step 1250 (0.084). At the final checkpoint, the accel_step probe (R2 = 0.917 at layer 1, control 0.742, margin 0.175) is stronger in absolute terms than the force probe (R2 = 0.729 at layer 4, control 0.507, margin 0.222). Distance (0.973 vs 0.769) and energy (0.832 vs 0.660) also beat their controls. Velocity does not (0.955 vs 0.878, margin 0.078 < 0.1).
confidence_note: The verdict covers only the stated hypothesis (val_mse_ratio < 1). The ratio of 0.005 sits about 200x below the threshold, so the result is not borderline, but it comes from one seed and one data seed. A second seed with val_mse_ratio >= 1 would be needed to overturn it, which is unlikely given the size of the gap. The probe results add context but are weak evidence on their own. The random-model controls are high (0.51-0.88), so much of each target is linearly readable from the input encoding. Force and accel_step both scale as 1/r^2 and are correlated across this dataset, so this run cannot say which one the model encodes. Force has the larger margin over control but the lower R2, and it peaks at a different layer (4 vs 1). Probes were run only at the final checkpoint, so formed_at_step = 5000 means 'present at the last checkpoint', not 'formed at step 5000'.

claim: The 4-layer transformer beat constant-velocity extrapolation on held-out two-body systems by about 200x: val_mse_ratio = 0.0051 (MSE 1.31e-7 vs baseline 2.55e-5), and the ratio stayed below 1 from step 500 onward (0.354 at step 500). Secondary probe readout at the final checkpoint: force R2 = 0.728 at layer 2 vs control 0.526 (margin 0.20), distance R2 = 0.967 vs 0.655, energy R2 = 0.791 vs 0.538, and velocity R2 = 0.952 vs control 0.888, which falls short of the 0.1 margin; accel_step was not probed, so we can't tell whether the force signal reflects physical force or the per-snapshot version.
confidence_note: Only one seed (seed 0) on one dataset (data_seed 0), so this is weak evidence, although the effect is large: the ratio is about 200x below the threshold of 1. With N = 64 snapshots per orbit and e <= 0.5, the constant-velocity baseline is weak, so beating it shows good next-step prediction, not that the model learned the physical law. The validation curve was not monotonic (0.098 at step 1000, 0.142 at step 1250; 0.043 at 2250, 0.053 at 2750), but it never came near 1. Probes were run only at the final checkpoint, so formed_at_step = 5000 says nothing about when the structure formed. The verdict would change if replication with other seeds or data seeds gave val_mse_ratio >= 1, or if the result failed to hold on out-of-distribution eval sets (higher eccentricity, different mass ratios).
